from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Scene
        lecture_lines = [
            "How do we find Pi using only simple fractions?",
            "Consider the Wallis Formula as an infinite product.",
            "It approaches Pi halves using ratios of integers."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: Finding Pi without a Compass", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color change for current line
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#F4D03F")
        
        # Fade in a bright blue circle (#58C4DD) with 'Area = pi' (#FFFFFF) inside.
        # Replacing MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color="#58C4DD", fill_opacity=0.6)
        area_label = Text("Area = π", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=36)
        
        # Anchor in the middle of the right side grid area
        self.place_in_area(circle, "B2", "E5")
        self.place_in_area(area_label, "B2", "E5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(circle), FadeIn(area_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Shift highlighting
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#F4D03F")
        
        # Replacing MathTex with Text for all mathematical symbols
        pi_half = Text("π / 2", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(pi_half, "B1", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        eq_sign = Text("=", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(eq_sign, "B2", scale_factor=1.2)

        # ratios '2/1' and '2/3' appear (#F4D03F).
        r1 = Text("2/1", color="#F4D03F", font_size=32)
        dot1 = Text("·", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=36)
        r2 = Text("2/3", color="#F4D03F", font_size=32)
        
        # Grouping for consistent horizontal alignment
        ratio_grp_1 = VGroup(r1, dot1, r2).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.15)
        self.place_at_grid(ratio_grp_1, "B4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(circle, pi_half),
            FadeOut(area_label),
            FadeIn(eq_sign),
            FadeIn(ratio_grp_1)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Shift highlighting
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#F4D03F")
        
        # A sequence of ratios grows horizontally
        dot2 = Text("·", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=36)
        r3 = Text("4/3", color="#F4D03F", font_size=32)
        dot3 = Text("·", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=36)
        r4 = Text("4/5", color="#F4D03F", font_size=32)
        dots = Text("...", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=32)
        
        ratio_grp_2 = VGroup(dot2, r3, dot3, r4, dots).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.15)
        # Position it to continue the horizontal line
        self.place_in_area(ratio_grp_2, "C1", "C6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Reaching the value 1.5707 (#FFFFFF)
        approx = Text("≈", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(approx, "D1", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # DecimalNumber uses Text-based logic to avoid latex dependency
        value_display = DecimalNumber(
            0,
            num_decimal_places=4,
            include_sign=False,
            color="#FFFFFF",
            mob_class=Text
        )
        self.place_at_grid(value_display, "D2", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(ratio_grp_2))
        self.play(FadeIn(approx), FadeIn(value_display))
        self.play(
            value_display.animate.set_value(1.5707),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=bezier([0, 0, 1, 1])
        )
        self.wait(3)

class Section2Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Layout
        title_text = "The Wallis Product: Unveiling Pi"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Infinite Product Representation",
            "- Derivation via Integration",
            "- Relationship to Pi/2",
            "- Convergence Analysis"
        ]

        # 2. Add Title
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(title)

        # 3. Create Left-side Bullet Points
        lecture_vgroup = VGroup(*[
            Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) 
            for line in lecture_lines
        ]).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        
        lecture_vgroup.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5)
        self.add(lecture_vgroup)

        # 4. Define Right-side Grid Logic (6x6)
        # We manually calculate positions to ensure compatibility with 0.19.0
        grid_positions = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Right-side bias: x starts from 1.0, y starts from 2.0
                x_pos = 1.0 + (j * 0.8)
                y_pos = 2.0 - (i * 0.8)
                grid_positions[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x_pos, y_pos, 0])

        # 5. Visual Elements for Demonstration
        # Wallis Product Formula at B3
        # FIXED: Replaced MathTex with Text using Unicode characters to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        formula = Text(
            "π/2 = ∏ [ 2n/(2n-1) · 2n/(2n+1) ]",
            font_size=26,
            color=YELLOW
        )
        formula.move_to(grid_positions["B3"] + RIGHT * 0.5)

        # Visual aid at D5
        box = Rectangle(height=1.5, width=2.0, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        box.move_to(grid_positions["D5"])
        
        circle = Circle(radius=0.4, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.6)
        circle.move_to(grid_positions["D5"])

        # 6. Animations
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.play(FadeIn(lecture_vgroup, shift=RIGHT))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(Create(box))
        self.play(FadeIn(circle, scale=0.5))
        
        self.wait(3)

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_dict, pos_key, scale_val=1.0):
        """Helper method for manual placement if needed in expansion"""
        mobject.scale(scale_val)
        mobject.move_to(grid_dict[pos_key])
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "Even vs. Odd: The Convergence Logic", 
            [
                "Even and odd terms form two distinct sequences.", 
                "As n goes to infinity, their ratio approaches one.", 
                "The difference between these sequences becomes negligible."
            ]
        )
        
        # Colors based on visual flow requirements
        COLOR_EVEN_ODD = "#58C4DD"
        COLOR_RATIO = "#F4D03F"
        COLOR_INEQUALITY = "#FF7043"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_EVEN_ODD))
        
        # Split screen labels
        even_header = Text("Even", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        odd_header = Text("Odd", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(even_header, "A1", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(odd_header, "A6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Column separator line between columns 3 and 4
        sep_start = (self.grid["A3"] + self.grid["A4"]) / 2 + UP * 0.4
        sep_end = (self.grid["E3"] + self.grid["E4"]) / 2 + DOWN * 0.4
        separator = Line(sep_start, sep_end, color=WHITE)
        
        # Sequences (Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependency)
        even_terms = VGroup(
            Text("I_0", color=COLOR_EVEN_ODD, font_size=32),
            Text("I_2", color=COLOR_EVEN_ODD, font_size=32),
            Text("I_4", color=COLOR_EVEN_ODD, font_size=32)
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.6)
        
        odd_terms = VGroup(
            Text("I_1", color=COLOR_EVEN_ODD, font_size=32),
            Text("I_3", color=COLOR_EVEN_ODD, font_size=32),
            Text("I_5", color=COLOR_EVEN_ODD, font_size=32)
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.6)
        
        self.place_at_grid(even_terms, "C1", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(odd_terms, "C6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(even_header), 
            FadeIn(odd_header), 
            Create(separator), 
            FadeIn(even_terms), 
            FadeIn(odd_terms)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_RATIO))
        
        # Show ratio representation
        ratio_tex = Text("I(2n) / I(2n-1) → 1", color=COLOR_RATIO, font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(ratio_tex, "B3", "D4", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(ratio_tex))
        
        # Number line at the bottom - explicitly use Text to avoid LaTeX
        num_line = NumberLine(
            x_range=[0.5, 1.5, 0.25],
            length=4.5,
            color=WHITE,
            include_numbers=True,
            font_size=18,
            numbers_to_include=[0.5, 1.0, 1.5],
            label_constructor=Text
        )
        self.place_in_area(num_line, "F1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Ratio movement indicator
        ratio_tracker = ValueTracker(1.4)
        pointer = Arrow(UP, DOWN, color=COLOR_RATIO, buff=0).scale(0.4)
        pointer.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(num_line.n2p(ratio_tracker.get_value()), UP, buff=0.1))
        
        # Explicitly use Text as mob_class to avoid LaTeX
        val_label = DecimalNumber(
            1.4, 
            num_decimal_places=2, 
            color=COLOR_RATIO, 
            font_size=20,
            mob_class=Text
        )
        val_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_value(ratio_tracker.get_value()).next_to(pointer, UP, buff=0.1))
        
        self.play(Create(num_line))
        self.add(pointer, val_label)
        self.play(ratio_tracker.animate.set_value(1.0), run_time=3, rate_func=smooth)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_INEQUALITY))
        
        # Display the monotonicity inequality
        inequality = Text("I(2n) > I(2n+1) > I(2n+2)", color=COLOR_INEQUALITY, font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(inequality, "E1", "E6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(inequality))
        # Visual flash for emphasis
        self.play(Flash(inequality, color=COLOR_INEQUALITY, line_length=0.4))
        self.play(
            inequality.animate.scale(1.1),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=0.4
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "The Final Product: Piecing it Together"
        lines = [
            "Combine even and odd sequences to isolate Pi.",
            "Expansion creates a chain of fractions like LEGO bricks.",
            "Two over one, times two over three...",
            "This product converges slowly to Pi halves.",
            "Watch the value approach one point five seven."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        even_product = Text(
            "I_2k = (2k-1)/2k · (2k-3)/(2k-2) · ... · 1/2 · π/2",
            color=WHITE, font_size=24
        )
        self.place_in_area(even_product, "A1", "A6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(even_product))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#58C4DD")
        odd_product = Text(
            "I_2k+1 = 2k/(2k+1) · (2k-2)/(2k-1) · ... · 2/3",
            color="#58C4DD", font_size=24
        )
        self.place_in_area(odd_product, "B1", "B6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(odd_product))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#F4D03F")
        
        lego_fractions = ["2/1", "2/3", "4/3", "4/5", "6/5", "6/7"]
        lego_group = VGroup()
        for i, frac_tex in enumerate(lego_fractions):
            box = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=0.8, height=0.6, color="#F4D03F", fill_opacity=0.2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial layout setup
        lecture_lines = [
            "This product is fundamental in probability and physics.",
            "It relates to Stirling's approximation and hydrogen atoms.",
            "Simple fractions reveal the universe's hidden clockwork."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Application: Why It Matters", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight line 1
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW), run_time=0.5)

        # Wallis Product Formula - Fixed using Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        wallis_formula = Text(
            "pi/2 = product (4n^2 / (4n^2-1))",
            color=WHITE,
            font_size=24
        )
        self.place_in_area(wallis_formula, "B1", "C3", scale_factor=0.6)

        # Stirling's Approximation - Fixed using Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        stirling_formula = Text(
            "n! ~ sqrt(2*pi*n) * (n/e)^n",
            color=WHITE,
            font_size=24
        )
        self.place_in_area(stirling_formula, "B4", "C6", scale_factor=0.6)

        self.play(
            FadeIn(wallis_formula),
            FadeIn(stirling_formula)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight line 2, reset line 1
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            run_time=0.5
        )

        # Hydrogen Atom Model
        nucleus = Dot(point=ORIGIN, color=WHITE, radius=0.08)
        
        # Create an electron orbit and electron
        orbit_1 = Ellipse(width=1.5, height=0.6, color="#58C4DD", stroke_width=1).rotate(45*DEGREES)
        orbit_2 = Ellipse(width=1.5, height=0.6, color="#58C4DD", stroke_width=1).rotate(-45*DEGREES)
        
        electron_1 = Dot(color="#58C4DD", radius=0.04)
        electron_2 = Dot(color="#58C4DD", radius=0.04)
        
        # Path follow functions
        def update_electron_1(m, dt):
            m.val += dt * 0.5
            m.move_to(orbit_1.point_from_proportion(m.val % 1))
            
        def update_electron_2(m, dt):
            m.val += dt * 0.7
            m.move_to(orbit_2.point_from_proportion(m.val % 1))

        electron_1.val = 0
        electron_2.val = 0.5
        electron_1.add_updater(update_electron_1)
        electron_2.add_updater(update_electron_2)

        atom_group = VGroup(nucleus, orbit_1, orbit_2, electron_1, electron_2)
        self.place_in_area(atom_group, "D1", "F3", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(FadeIn(atom_group))
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight line 3, reset line 2
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            run_time=0.5
        )

        # Bell Curve (Normal Distribution)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3],
            y_range=[0, 1],
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "include_ticks": False, "stroke_width": 1},
            tips=False
        ).set_color(GRAY)
        
        bell_curve = axes.plot(
            lambda x: np.exp(-x**2), 
            color="#4CAF50",
            stroke_width=3
        )
        
        curve_group = VGroup(axes, bell_curve)
        self.place_in_area(curve_group, "D4", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)

        self.play(Create(bell_curve), FadeIn(axes))
        self.wait(4)

        # Final cleanup
        self.play(
            FadeOut(wallis_formula),
            FadeOut(stirling_formula),
            FadeOut(atom_group),
            FadeOut(curve_group),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: The Wallis Product: Unveiling Pi through Infinite Fractions
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students or advanced high school students with a basic understanding of calculus.

sections.title: The Hook: Finding Pi without a Compass
sections.content: Introduce the mystery: How can we calculate the area of a circle (Pi) using only a sequence of simple fractions? Present the Wallis Formula visually as a growing chain of ratios.
sections.example: Imagine 'Archie the Architect' trying to build a perfectly circular dome using only rectangular bricks labeled with even and odd numbers. He discovers that as he multiplies their ratios (2/1 * 2/3 * 4/3 * 4/5...), the result gets closer to Pi/2.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Wallis Integrals
sections.content: Introduce the function I_n = integral from 0 to π/2 of (sin x)^n dx. Use an animation to show how the area under the curve shrinks as the exponent 'n' increases.
sections.example: Show a graph of sin(x) vs sin^2(x) vs sin^10(x). The area starts as a large wave and progressively 'thins out' into a narrow spike near x = π/2.

sections.title: The Reduction Step: Building the Staircase
sections.content: Explain the recurrence relation: I_n = ((n-1)/n) * I_{n-2}. This connects a higher power of sine to a lower one, creating a downward 'staircase' of values.
sections.example: A visual staircase where jumping from step 'n' to 'n-2' involves multiplying by a specific fraction. For example, to get from the 4th step to the 2nd, you multiply by 3/4.

sections.title: Even vs. Odd: The Convergence Logic
sections.content: Compare the sequence of 'even' integrals (I_0, I_2, I_4...) and 'odd' integrals (I_1, I_3, I_5...). Explain that as n goes to infinity, the ratio between consecutive terms approaches 1.
sections.example: Think of two runners (Even Runner and Odd Runner). As they run further out (n → ∞), the distance between them becomes negligible, forcing their ratio to converge.

sections.title: The Final Product: Piecing it Together
sections.content: Combine the even and odd sequences to isolate π/2. Show the expansion: π/2 = (2/1 * 2/3) * (4/3 * 4/5) * (6/5 * 6/7)... and how it transforms into the Wallis Product.
sections.example: An animated assembly line where fractions (2/1, 2/3, 4/3, etc.) are clicked together like LEGO bricks. A digital counter nearby displays the value approaching 1.5707... (π/2).

sections.title: Application: Why It Matters
sections.content: Briefly explain that the Wallis product isn't just a curiosity; it's a precursor to Stirling's approximation and is used in probability and quantum physics (energy levels of the hydrogen atom).
sections.example: A quick visual flash of a Hydrogen atom and a bell curve, showing that this simple string of fractions is a hidden gear in the clockwork of the universe.

lecture_lines: Can we find Pi using only simple fractions?
A growing chain of ratios reveals Pi halves.
This infinite product converges to one point five seven.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Wallis Integrals
lecture_lines: We define the integral of sine to the nth power.
The area under sine starts as a large wave.
Increasing the exponent causes the area to shrink.
Higher powers narrow into a thin spike.
This specific area is denoted as I sub n.

storyboard.title: The Reduction Step: Building the Staircase
lecture_lines: Integration by parts reveals a helpful recurrence relation.
This creates a downward staircase of integral values.
Every jump down multiplies by a specific fraction.
animations: Show 'Integration by Parts' text and the resulting I_n formula in white (#FFFFFF).
Display 'I_n =' and '(n-1)/n' in a yellow box (#F4D03F).
Append 'I_{n-2}' to the yellow box to complete the recurrence formula.

storyboard.title: Even vs. Odd: The Convergence Logic
lecture_lines: Even and odd terms form two distinct sequences.
We compare terms from both sequences side by side.
Their ratios provide the key to convergence.
As n grows, the ratio approaches exactly one.
This squeeze effect forces the sequences to merge.
animations: Display sequences (I_0, I_2, I_4) and (I_1, I_3, I_5) in two distinct columns (#58C4DD).

storyboard.title: The Final Product: Piecing it Together
lecture_lines: Combine these sequences to isolate the value of Pi.
Fractions from both sequences begin to intertwine.
Rearranging these terms creates a chain of ratios.
We arrive at the elegant Wallis Product formula.
The numeric value converges slowly to Pi halves.
animations: Display the expanded forms of I_{2n} and I_{2n+1} in white (#FFFFFF) and blue (#58C4DD).
Rearrange terms to form the ratio I_{2n}/I_{2n+1}, isolating pi/2 on one side (#F4D03F).

Box the final Wallis Product formula in a bold white frame (#FFFFFF).
Display a running decimal total starting from 2.0 and converging to 1.5707 (#F4D03F).

storyboard.title: Application: Why It Matters
lecture_lines: This product links to Stirling's approximation of factorials.
It even appears in the physics of hydrogen atoms.
Simple fractions reveal the universe's hidden mathematical clockwork.
